statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-87863: an HTTPS server can send an HSTS max-age so large that curl later fails to write the entry's expiry date when it saves its HSTS cache file; the save then stops after the original file was truncated, leaving it empty or partial, and curl does not report the error (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-87863.html). It affects the curl tool and libcurl from 8.2.0 to 8.22.0 and was fixed in curl 8.23.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/08d50a791b3197a3d0a4fc2f778e243f5501c67e, which caps max-age at two years (63072000 seconds) and skips, rather than stopping at, an entry whose date cannot be written. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 published in the DHI Alpine main repository as of 2026-11-28 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the HSTS object of the static libcurl.a in curl-static and in Curl_hsts_parse in libcurl.so.4 in libcurl (located with the symbols in curl-dbg), on x86_64 and aarch64, the two-year cap 63072000 is loaded as a constant in 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1 and appears in no earlier build. 8.23.0-r0 is the first fixed build. Packages published only in the DHI Alpine security repository, which needs credentials, were not inspected.
